summary.intent: Add Phase 36 to the roadmap for refactoring upload progress from a popup modal to an inline display, then capture implementation context via a structured discussion workflow.
summary.outcome: Phase 36 created with a shortened slug (36-inline-upload-progress), feature branch renamed to feat/phase-36-inline-upload-progress, CONTEXT.md and DISCUSSION-LOG.md written with 5 locked decisions, and all files committed cleanly.

repo: The gsd-tools `phase add` command generates slugs directly from the full description string — no truncation, resulting in absurdly long directory names for verbose descriptions.
The gsd commit script (`gsd-tools commit`) creates its own branch naming convention that can diverge from a manually created branch, causing branch proliferation.
The cipher-box web app uses UploadModal.tsx and UploadItem.tsx for the current popup upload progress UI — these are targeted for deletion in Phase 36.
Zustand store pattern is the established state management approach across all phases.
Terminal aesthetic UI is a non-negotiable design constraint carried across all phases.
The SDK upload pipeline (encrypt → IPFS → register) is out of scope for this phase — only the progress display layer changes.
A pending todo 'Offload large file encryption to Web Worker' exists with high relevance (0.9) to upload but was explicitly deferred as a separate concern from progress display.
workflow: When using `/gsd:add-phase`, keep the description short — the full description becomes the directory slug verbatim.
After renaming a phase directory manually, git treats it as delete + untracked rather than a rename, requiring explicit staging of both the deletion and the new path.
The gsd commit tool may silently create or switch branches as a side effect — always verify branch state after using it with `git status` and `git branch`.
discuss-phase workflow in 'discuss' mode presents gray areas interactively and captures decisions across: placement, per-file detail, lifecycle/dismissal, and cancel/error UX.

friction: gsd-tools `phase add` generated a 110+ character directory slug from the full phase description with no truncation or length guard.

The gsd commit script created a divergent branch (`phase-36-inline-upload-progress`) instead of committing on the existing `feat/inline-upload-progress` branch, requiring manual branch cleanup and rename.
Directory rename (mv) left unstaged deletions of old files and untracked new .gitkeep, requiring a separate cleanup commit — the rename wasn't atomic from git's perspective.
No `gsd-tools phase rename` command exists, forcing a manual multi-step rename: mv directory, grep+edit ROADMAP.md, edit CONTEXT.md and DISCUSSION-LOG.md references.
open_items: Web Worker encryption offload todo (relevance 0.9) explicitly deferred — not part of Phase 36 scope.
Phase 36 implementation not started — CONTEXT.md captured, next step is `/gsd:plan-phase 36`.
Consider adding slug truncation or a `--slug` override flag to gsd-tools `phase add` to prevent verbose directory names.
Consider adding a `gsd-tools phase rename` subcommand to handle the multi-file rename atomically.
